question.worked_solution:
We note that $f=0$ cannot be a solution since division by $0$ is undefined. 

The equation has the denominators $f,\,2f,$ and $5f.$ So first, we find the least common multiple (or $\text{LCM}$) of the denominators. We find that

$$
\text{LCM}(f,2f,5f)=10f.
$$

So, we multiply both sides of the equation by $10f,$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{f+6}{f}-\frac{3f+9}{5f} & =\frac{f+2}{2f} \\ 10f(\frac{f+6}{f}-\frac{3f+9}{5f}) & =10f(\frac{f+2}{2f}) \\ 10f\cdot \frac{f+6}{f}-10f\cdot \frac{3f+9}{5f} & =10f\cdot \frac{f+2}{2f} \\ 10\cdot f\cdot \frac{f+6}{f}-2\cdot 5f\cdot \frac{3f+9}{5f} & =5\cdot 2f\cdot \frac{f+2}{2f} \\ 10\cdot \cancel{f}\cdot \frac{f+6}{\cancel{f}}-2\cdot \cancel{5f}\cdot \frac{3f+9}{\cancel{5f}} & =5\cdot \cancel{2f}\cdot \frac{f+2}{\cancel{2f}} \\ 10(f+6)-2(3f+9) & =5(f+2)\end{aligned}
$$

We now have a linear equation in $f,$ and we can solve this using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}10(f+6)-2(3f+9) & =5(f+2) \\ 10f+60-6f-18 & =5f+10 \\ 4f+42 & =5f+10 \\ -f & =-32 \\ f & =32\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we recall that we cannot allow $f=0$ as a solution. But since $f=32\ne 0,$ we conclude that the solution is $f=32.$
